title: Customer Lifecycle
summary: Customer = 5-stage journey; improve the weakest stage before increasing traffic.

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? A customer is not just a single transaction — it is a Customer Journey from the first time they hear about you until they recommend you. AI can enhance every stage.
- Why now? After distinguishing between Reactive and Proactive business approaches, we move to the most important part of any business: the Customer Journey.
- What comes after the lesson? You will map a real Customer Journey — and identify the Weakest Stage.

sections.heading: Tension — A Familiar Situation
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Many see a customer as «bought and done». They bring in new customers through ads — but the return rate is low and costs are rising.
- The problem is often not «we need more ads» — the issue lies in a weak stage in the journey: Awareness, Consideration, Purchase, Retention, or Advocacy.
- AI helps you map the journey and write follow-up messages — but you need to know where the leak is.

sections.heading: Core Idea — 5 Stages — Each Stage is an Opportunity
sections.subtitle: 5 Stages — Each Stage is an Opportunity
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Awareness: The customer knows you exist — through an ad, a friend, or a search.
- Consideration: They compare — price, trust, reviews.
- Purchase: The first transaction — the experience here determines if they return.
- Retention: They come back a second time — follow-up, recurring value.
- Advocacy: They tell others — cheaper than a new ad.
- AI helps in crafting messages for each stage — but diagnosis starts with mapping the real journey.

sections.heading: Glossary — Two Terms for the Journey
sections.subtitle: Two Terms for the Journey
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|------|--------|--------|
| Customer Journey | All stages from the first time they hear about you until they recommend you | Post → Inquiry → Order → Follow-up → Return → Recommendation |
| Weakest Stage | The stage where most people drop off | 60% buy once and do not return — the weakness is often in Retention, not Awareness |

sections.heading: Comparison — More Ads vs Fixing a Stage
sections.subtitle: More Ads vs Fixing a Stage
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Focus on bringing in new customers only | Fix the weakest stage |
|------------------------|-----------------|
| Increase ads — new customers come — but the same percentage do not return — costs rise | Map the journey — discover that follow-up after purchase is weak — a simple message + AI — the same customers return more |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: A business brings in 100 new customers monthly — only 15 return. What is the best initial focus?
Improve the Retention stage — why do those who bought not return?
Explanation: Bringing in a new customer is often more expensive than getting an existing customer to return. If the weakness is in return rates — start with retention before increasing ads.

sections.heading: Mission — Map a Customer Journey — Identify Weakness
sections.subtitle: Map a Customer Journey — Identify Weakness
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: An application to your business — not theory. Map a real customer journey through the five stages. Then identify the Weakest Stage and why. Submission: Awareness · Consideration · Purchase · Retention · Advocacy · Weakest Stage + reason Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Realistic Journey | 60% | The five stages are linked to your business — no general definitions |
| Weakness Diagnosis | 40% | A specific weak stage with a logical reason |
